# claude-bughunter

> A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **84 skills** · 15 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com).

Built by **Sachin Sharma** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

 
   SPONSORED BY 
   
   
   
     
       
       
     
   
        
   
     
       
       
     
   
 

---

## What is this?

`claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the Claude Code skills system. Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope.

Four layers stack:

- **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline.
- **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates.
- **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation.
- **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables.

All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name.

---

## Quickstart

**Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls
```

All 84 skills + 15 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`.

**A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them.

git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git
cd Claude-BugHunter
```

# macOS / Linux
bash scripts/install.sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1
```

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

   "大道至简" 
 

 

中文 | English

 

* 此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。
* MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。
* 项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。
* MiniMind 同时拓展了视觉模态模型 MiniMind-V、多模态 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O、扩散语言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、线性模型（MiniMind-Linear），详见 Discussion。
* 项目所有核心算法代码均从 0 使用 PyTorch 原生实现，不依赖第三方库提供的高层抽象接口。
* 这不仅是一个大语言模型全阶段开源复现项目，也是一套面向 LLM 入门与实践的教程。
* 希望此项目能为更多人提供一个可复现、可理解、可扩展的起点，一起感受创造的乐趣，并推动更广泛 AI 社区的进步。

> 注：本项目基于 Apache 2.0 协议开源，完全免费。“2 小时” 指 SFT 阶段在单张 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 `1 epoch` 的实测耗时，“3 块钱” 指对应时段的 GPU 租用成本。

# 📌 项目介绍

大语言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出现，引发了全球范围内对 AI 的空前关注。无论是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 还是 Qwen，都以惊艳的效果让人真切感受到这场技术浪潮的冲击力。然而，动辄数百亿参数的模型规模，使得它们对个人设备而言不仅难以训练，甚至连部署都显得遥不可及。打开大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其内部运作机制，本应是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遗憾的是，绝大多数探索最终都止步于使用 LoRA 等技术对现有大模型做少量微调，学习一些新指令或特定任务。这更像是在教牛顿如何使用 21 世纪的智能手机——虽然有趣，却偏离了理解物理本质的初衷。

与此同时，第三方的大模型框架与工具库，如 `transformers` / `trl` / `peft` 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的接口。只需短短十几行代码，就可以完成“加载模型 + 加载数据集 + 推理 + 强化学习”的全流程训练。这种高效封装固然便利，却也在一定程度上把开发者与底层实现隔离开来，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心代码的机会。我认为 “用乐高自己拼出一架飞机，远比坐在头等舱里飞行更让人兴奋”，然而更现实的问题是，互联网上充斥着大量付费课程和营销内容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的讲解包装所谓的 AI 教程。正因如此，本项目的初衷就是尽可能降低 LLM 的学习门槛，让每个人都能从理解每一行代码开始，从 0 开始亲手训练一个极小的语言模型。是的，从**零开始训练**，而不是仅仅停留在**推理**层面。最低只需不到 3 块钱的服务器成本，就能亲身体验从 0 到 1 构建一个语言模型的全过程。

😊 一起感受创造的乐趣吧！

- 提供 Tokenizer 与分词器训练代码，支持 ` `、` `、` ` 等模板标记。

- 提供全阶段开源数据，覆盖收集、蒸馏、清洗与去重后的高质量数据集。
- 关键训练算法与核心模块均从 0 实现，不依赖第三方框架封装。
- 兼容 `transformers`、`trl`、`peft` 等主流框架，以及 `llama.cpp`、`vllm`、`ollama` 等常用推理引擎与 `Llama-Factory` 等训练框架。
- 支持单机单卡与单机多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）训练，支持 wandb / swanlab 可视化与动态启停训练。
- 支持在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方测评集上进行评测，并支持通过 YaRN 实现 RoPE 长文本外推。

# **🔥 Firecrawl**

**Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥** You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three.

- **Firecrawl Local.** Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost.
- **Firecrawl Cloud.** Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone.
- **Self-hosting.** Deploy the full Firecrawl server from `apps/api` with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure.

_Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)_

 
   
 

---

## Firecrawl Local

Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means `xcode-select --install` and on Debian or Ubuntu means `build-essential`.

```bash
cargo install firecrawl-local
```

If you don't have Rust, Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup.

```bash
npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev
```

Scrape a page and print its markdown.

```bash
firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown
```

Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page.

```bash
firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages
```

List every URL on a site.

```bash
firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev
```

Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning.

### Add it to your AI agent

`init` finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer.

```bash
firecrawl-local init
```

Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud.

### Run the Firecrawl API on localhost

`serve` answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key.

```bash
firecrawl-local serve
```

NGINX (pronounced "engine x" or "en-jin-eks") is the world's most popular Web Server, high performance Load Balancer, Reverse Proxy, API Gateway and Content Cache.

NGINX is free and open source software, distributed under the terms of a simplified 2-clause BSD-like license.

Enterprise distributions, commercial support and training are available from F5, Inc.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The goal of this README is to provide a basic, structured introduction to NGINX for novice users. Please refer to the full NGINX documentation for detailed information on installing, building, configuring, debugging, and more. These documentation pages also contain a more detailed Beginners Guide, How-Tos, Development guide, and a complete module and directive reference.

NGINX is installed software with binary packages available for all major operating systems and Linux distributions. See Tested OS and Platforms for a full list of compatible systems.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> While nearly all popular Linux-based operating systems are distributed with a community version of nginx, we highly advise installation and usage of official packages or sources from this repository. Doing so ensures that you're using the most recent release or source code, including the latest feature-set, fixes and security patches.

## Modules
NGINX is comprised of individual modules, each extending core functionality by providing additional, configurable features. See "Modules reference" at the bottom of nginx documentation for a complete list of official modules.

NGINX modules can be built and distributed as static or dynamic modules. Static modules are defined at build-time, compiled, and distributed in the resulting binaries. See Dynamic Modules for more information on how they work, as well as, how to obtain, install, and configure them.

```bash
nginx -V

items.content:
Open-source software toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models.
 

 
   Documentation   •   Blog   •   Key Features   •   Tutorials   •   Integrations   •   Benchmarks   •   Generative AI  
 

[](https://badge.fury.io/py/openvino)

[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openvino)
  

- **Inference Optimization**: Boost deep learning performance in computer vision, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, natural language processing with large and small language models, and many other common tasks.
- **Flexible Model Support**: Use models trained with popular frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax. Directly integrate models built with transformers and diffusers from the Hugging Face Hub using Optimum Intel. Convert and deploy models without original frameworks.
- **Broad Platform Compatibility**: Reduce resource demands and efficiently deploy on a range of platforms from edge to cloud. OpenVINO™ supports inference on CPU (x86, ARM), GPU (Intel integrated & discrete GPU) and AI accelerators (Intel NPU).
- **Community and Ecosystem**: Join an active community contributing to the enhancement of deep learning performance across various domains.

Check out the OpenVINO Cheat Sheet and Key Features for a quick reference.

## Installation

Get your preferred distribution of OpenVINO or use this command for quick installation:

```sh
pip install -U openvino
```

### Verify Installation

After installation, you can verify OpenVINO is installed correctly by running:

```python
import openvino as ov
print(ov.__version__)
```

Check system requirements and supported devices for detailed information.

## Tutorials and Examples

OpenVINO Quickstart example will walk you through the basics of deploying your first model.

Learn how to optimize and deploy popular models with the OpenVINO Notebooks 📚:
- Create an LLM-powered Chatbot using OpenVINO
- YOLOv11 Optimization
- Text-to-Image Generation
- Multimodal assistant with LLaVa and OpenVINO
- Automatic speech recognition using Whisper and OpenVINO

Discover more examples in the OpenVINO Samples (Python & C++) and Notebooks (Python).

Here are easy-to-follow code examples demonstrating how to run PyTorch and TensorFlow model inference using OpenVINO:

**PyTorch Model**

```python
import openvino as ov
import torch
import torchvision

# load PyTorch model into memory

# convert the model into OpenVINO model

ov_model = ov.convert_model(model, example_input=(example,))

# compile the model for CPU device
core = ov.Core()
compiled_model = core.compile_model(ov_model, 'CPU')

items.title: 养猫两个月，我和猫的关系却越来越糟
items.summary:
养猫新手，捡了一只狸白，现在 7～8 个月大，养了快两个月。

刚开始相处得其实挺好，猫也比较亲人，偶尔翻垃圾桶、上蹿下跳，犯一些小错误，我也会呵斥他。

真正的转折点是有一次他挠到了我，我动手打了他。

从那以后，他开始逐渐害怕我。原本亲近的关系慢慢变了，我想抱他，他开始躲；我靠近他，他有时会哈气。

更糟糕的是，我们逐渐形成了一个恶性循环：他因为害怕而躲避、哈气，我看到这种反应就容易生气，忍不住呵斥甚至动手；而这些行为又让他更加害怕我。下一次遇到类似的情况，矛盾只会进一步升级。

我也开始反思，猫哈气、躲避究竟是不是正常的防御行为？是不是我根本就不应该把这些行为理解成挑衅或者不服管教？

但网上的信息实在太混乱了。抖音、小红书上有人说千万不能打，有人说猫就是要管教，甚至有人认为打、饿、关都是必要的。AI 给出的建议又几乎都是顺其自然、不要强迫、给猫时间。

我现在反而不知道应该相信谁，也不知道自己之前是不是被网上的一些错误观念带偏了。

我承认，问题很大程度上出在我自己身上。我不是不想和他好好相处，也不是不在乎他，而是有时候控制不住自己的情绪，把猫正常的防御反应理解成了对我的挑衅。或者我这样理解到底正确吗？也许他这个反应就应该得到相应的惩戒？

我承认，问题很大程度上出在我自己身上。我不是不想和他好好相处，也不是不在乎他，而是有时候控制不住自己的情绪，把猫正常的防御反应理解成了对我的挑衅。或者我这样理解到底正确吗？也许他这个反应就应该得到相应的惩戒？ 希望有实际养猫经验的人能给一些真正可操作的建议，而不是简单地说一句顺其自然，或者一味强调打与不打。 Supplement 1  · 1h 33m ago items.title: 2026 年我的常用 Mac 软件分享
items.summary:
![2026 我的 Mac 常用软件，按自己做的、产品开发、上网、效率四组排列的 24 个软件图标](https://cdn.tw93.fun/blog/pic/mac-apps-2026.webp)

每年固定节目，给大伙分享我这一年每天都在用的不错 Mac 软件，由于有了 AI 以后反而常用软件少了很多，只有这 24 个了，看看哪些是大伙也经常在用的，也欢迎推荐你认为 2026 你最喜欢的软件给我。

打算想到啥说啥，先看到哪一个说哪个，不按照上图顺序来给大伙分享。

1. [**Mole**](https://mole.fit/)：几乎每天会用来清理一遍垃圾以及看菜单栏看系统的状态，包括里面的卸载、不息屏、风扇小工具每天会使用，同时每天都会来迭代它。
2. [**Claude Code**](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code)：我现在主要用 CLI，几乎每时每刻都在跑，默认 Opus 5.5 high，复杂就 Fable 5.2 medium，现在没有用 Codex 了，也没有用啥多 Agent 工具，我喜欢简单可控的编码。
3. [**Kaku**](https://kaku.fun/)：我喜欢简单默认好看轻量的终端工具，每天在上面多 Tab 跑 Claude，我喜欢用黑色背景的 TUI 搭配 [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/) 代码字体，这个字体依然是我最近三年最喜欢的代码字体。
4. [**ego lite**](https://lite.ego.app/)：今年最让我惊喜的一个浏览器，简单漂亮好用，之前我主要是用 [Helium Browser](https://helium.computer/)，假如你很少用 AI 操作浏览器，那我还是推荐 Helium 这个，轻量迅速简洁，ego 这个我喜欢的点，就有给 Agent 一个单独的窗口，不会干扰我自己的使用。
5. [**1Password**](https://1password.com/)：今年把我的密码管理逐步迁移到了这个，多平台复用，整体软件品质不错，更多是在 AI 什么都可以破解的年代求一份安全保障，价格也可以接受，用习惯以后，感觉还挺好用的。
6. [**妙言**](https://miaoyan.app/)：一个轻快的原生的 Markdown 笔记应用，默认好用好看，在支持 iPhone 版本后，我几乎每天会打开记录一些东西，每周大伙看到的[潮流周刊](https://weekly.tw93.fun/)就是我用这个 Mac 端来编辑的，包括大伙看到的我的所有文字输出，都是在这个里面草稿来的。
7. [**Grok Bot**](https://x.ai/bot)：可能不是每一个小伙伴喜欢用这个，我感觉他帮了我很多产品经营增长上的忙，包括各种答疑、退款处理、记录问题到 Notion，以及我每天的投资报告、推特日报、潮流日报，均来源于这个帮我在做 Personal Agent。
8. [**UU 远程**](https://uuyc.163.com/)：我感觉这个产品简单易用，在我外出的时候，非常依赖他帮我操作家里的多 Mac 和 Windows 设备，给我帮了很多忙，虽然后面也做付费了，不过我还是非常希望他家可以越做越好。
9. [**Apple Music**](https://www.apple.com.cn/apple-music/)：用过非常多音乐播放器，我还是最喜欢苹果自带的，包月也便宜，歌的质量也高，我听的歌也都在上面，而且我喜欢这个简洁，以及多设备使用，不太喜欢花里胡哨的东西，这个刚刚好。
10. [**Pake**](https://pake.run/)：一个可以很简单把网页打包成桌面 App 的工具，我会把微信读书、李志音乐播放器打包成 Mac 应用，然后用 Raycast 快捷键唤起，很方便，而且可以按照自己喜好定制非常多的东西。
11. [**Shottr**](https://shottr.cc/)：假如要推荐一个最好用最简单的截图工具，还是推荐这个，貌似才 4 刀不买好像也可以用，轻量、我非常喜欢用他来截图窗口、以及滚动截图，用了好几年了。
12. [**微信输入法**](https://z.weixin.qq.com/)：我的所有设备都是用这个输入法，腾讯的赎罪产品，简洁舒服、打字猜的准，特别是最近的语音输入法，我不想装同类的软件，就只用这个，非常好用。
13. [**Parallels**](https://www.parallels.com/)：这个软件可能对大伙也褒贬不一，但是我感觉还是这个 Windows 虚拟机做得最好用，也可能是我 M5 Pro 的缘故，我在上面用，完全没有虚拟机的感觉，非常顺滑，在我开发 Windows 软件的时候帮了很大的忙。
14. [**Bob**](https://bobtranslate.com/)：一个随手用的翻译工具，好像也不贵，然后绑定了自己的 AI key，设置快捷键以后，随用随唤起，很不错。
15. [**Input Source Pro**](https://inputsource.pro/)：默认切换输入法的工具，比如在你写东西的里面默认就是中文输入法，在你敲代码的地方默认设置英文，少掉了一次快捷键切换，润物细无声。
16. [**NetNewsWire**](https://netnewswire.com/)：轻量默认好用的 RSS 阅读器，也有 iPhone 版本，推荐使用我自己做的[妙言主题](https://github.com/tw93/MiaoYan-NetNewsWire-Theme)，很舒服，这是我认为在 AI 时代还需要保持阅读的一个很好工具。
17. [**Sketch**](https://www.sketch.com/)：哈哈好吧，我承认我现在的所有的设计、做 Logo、做稿子，还是用这个软件，可能是原生客户端的缘故，有执念，而且工具完全够我用，也比较舒服，可能是用习惯了，反而不太关注新产品。
18. [**Top Calendar**](https://guojiubo.github.io/zh/)：菜单栏最好用的日历时间插件，可以把系统的菜单栏时间替换后用这个，点击可以看到日历，以及你的日程，也是润物细无声。
19. [**AyuGram**](https://github.com/AyuGram/AyuGramDesktop)：开源易用简洁的电报工具，可以把原有官方的版本很多会员广告啥的干掉，然后有非常多自定义的功能，但是默认其实就够了，平时我每天打开 1-2 次看看消息。
20. [**Stash**](https://stash.ws/)：我在用的 Mac 和 iPhone 的代理工具，用了 2 年左右了，胜在稳定和原生，以及满足我使用的覆写、DNS 覆盖等功能，然后家里 Apple TV 也用的这个，我认为最好的就是多设备配置同步，省去了我来回配置的麻烦。
21. [**Raycast**](https://www.raycast.com/)：这个是唯一我感觉有点重但是也每天在用的工具，同步也在另外一台电脑上使用 [Tinycast](https://tinycast.dev/)，作为对照使用，Raycast 的粘贴历史记录、软件快捷键唤起、文件快捷键查找这几个功能我几乎每天用，就是麻烦一点第一次使用，你要关掉非常多我认为多余的功能才会好用，Tinycast 等更成熟了，可能主力机就迁移过去了。
22. [**uPic**](https://github.com/gee1k/uPic)：用了好多年的图片上传到 CDN 的工具，为啥用这个，还是原生轻量的执念，绑定好快捷键以后，我认为非常好用。
23. [**Command X**](https://sindresorhus.com/command-x)：一个非常轻量的让你的 Mac 在访达支持剪切的工具，就这个功能，哈哈哈。
24. [**VS Code**](https://code.visualstudio.com/)：前 AI 时代每天都在用的，现在也经常用，主要用来看一些 diff，以及整理一些文件内容，以及看 README，不过我感觉明年我可能就不用这个了，找一个更轻量原生的。

items.content: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI - by Ethan Mollick One Useful Thing Subscribe Sign in Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI General, often expert, and sometimes jagged Ethan Mollick Nov 09, 2026 1,505 252 178 Share Before getting started, I wanted to thank my readers for making my new book, Co-Existence, a New York Times bestseller two weeks in a row. If you haven’t read it, you can get a copy here . I have had the chance to use the new Claude Fable 5.2 quite a bit before its public launch 1 , and it is very impressive, following on the already excellent Opus 5.5. AI has gotten so good, in fact, that it is worth asking if Anthropic’s newest models (and the inevitable competing models OpenAI and Google will soon release) cross the boundary into being an Artificial General Intelligence? AGI is a much-debated term with a lot of potential definitions. For this post, I’ll go with: “an AI as good as most human experts at most intellectual tasks you can do with a computer.” This explicitly excludes a lot of human work, including interacting with the physical world and other people, as well as most actual jobs, where “using a computer” is just one task among many. Still, even with these caveats, building a limited form of AGI has long been the goal of AI developers. So as not to keep you in suspense, I think the answer is that this is “almost” AGI, or what I have called Jagged AGI. Even within my limited definition, there are still important areas in many tasks where AI is jagged enough to fall well behind human capability. But the jaggedness is no longer about simple errors or hallucinations, which makes it harder to describe. So I want to try to do that in this post by showing you what Fable can do and where the gaps are. To get started I asked the new model: “I write OneUsefulThing among other stuff, I need you to create the most impressive thing I can share with people when you launch. It needs to be embeddable in a post and i can preface it however you like. it needs to have a visceral impact on people to show what you can do and the range of capabilities. It should grab them quickly. Be amazingly clever about this.” Fable asked me not to reveal anything until you had watched its video to the end. This was in one shot, with no feedback from me beyond the prompt. There is creativity here (including in the twist ending) and judgment and playfulness and cleverness. This is, I think, at the level of a human expert trying to make a movie with code alone, the sort of performance I would once have associated with AGI. The “G” in AGI Code and video creation have been areas where AI development has focused, so is Fable 5.2 really a General Intelligence? items.content: 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts) - by Ethan Mollick One Useful Thing Subscribe Sign in 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts) My new book is out today... what happened since the last one Ethan Mollick Oct 20, 2026 823 148 70 Share My second book on AI, Co-Existence, is out today (and you can get it here ), 30 months after the release of Co-Intelligence in early 2024. Looking back across the gap between these books is a good way to get a sense of AI progress. And, thanks to AI, I can describe this progress with some quite lovely charts. Making the charts is itself a good indicator of how far things have come. In the era of chatbots, the era of Co-Intelligence , I would have had to work back-and-forth with an AI in a chat window, guiding it through each new step. In the current era of agentic AI that I cover in Co-Existence , I delegated the work and let the AI handle it. In this case, I used Opus 5.5 in Claude Projects, which allows you to talk to a single “orchestrator” agent that then spins off additional agents as needed, giving them instructions and relaying information back to you. Getting the work done was straightforward. I gave the AI a couple sentences of suggestions and it did what would have taken me hours of work (all the research, all the graphing, all the layouts, all the images, all the citations…) in minutes. And since I didn’t have to do the work, I had the AI make many options for me. I picked some and gave handwavy reactions to others that would drive a human team mad (“make it better”). It even caught that I’d gotten the math wrong. I was going to call this post “28 months on the exponential.” Some examples of interacting with Claude to make the graphics for this post. From early 2023 through early 2024, there was a single AI model that was undeniably the best in the world: GPT-4 from OpenAI. This was the AI model that most people remember from the first couple years of AI use, it was the one I thought about while writing Co-Intelligence , and it was the one that gave ChatGPT its status as the default AI for many people. Since then, twenty different AI models have held the lead at one time or another, all from Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI. Which company had the best AI model in the world. But the changing lead alone hides an even bigger change. A total of 180 AI models are now better than GPT-4 was at its release, many of which are open weights models, which anyone is free to use or modify. Nineteen of them can run on a modern smartphone. The Bitter Lesson is everywhere among AI startups and companies adopting AI. A huge amount of effort went into building elaborate computer systems to feed AIs the right information at the right time, but AI systems have learned to seek out information themselves. The same thing happened to prompting. People built elaborate templates and chains of prompts that walked the AI through a task one step at a time. items.content: Productiv-icky - by Ben Tossell - Ben's Bites Ben’s Bites Subscribe Sign in Productiv-icky Digging holes on the beach Ben Tossell Nov 17, 2026 79 4 2 Share productiv-icky (adj.) - the feeling of doing work you didn’t mean to do We have a problem. full interactive post is here We agree this is insane, right? Someone I don’t know sends me emails that I’m expected to reply to. I don’t know them. I don’t work for them. So I ignore them (well actually I send them to email jail). Nuh-uh, that’s not my work, buddy. But it’s different if it’s my super-intelligent, helpful agent friend… Yeses are easy. They’re quick. But every yes has a yes-tax. The hidden extra work you didn’t think of. The long tail of regret where you question why you ever said yes. Say I did reply to those emails, they’d send me stuff to read to show how great they are at their job and how much better I’d be. Then we’d organise a call (which would derail whichever day that call was on). Then we’d have follow-up items. Then a string of other crap I couldn’t care less about. I know what’s going to happen. I can smell it, it stinks. I’ve said yes and paid the tax many times before. Now I pay $200/mo for a super-intelligent, over-eager, needy little nerd to ping me incessantly about taking things off my plate. I feel bad for him. He wants to work. He’s gagging for it. Just. One. More. Task. Master. Plus, my little nerd has a gambling problem. Or rather, he feeds mine. Remember years ago sending tons of Slack messages to get the most out of your $20/mo plan? Nor me. Why? Because it’s dumb. But now we feel like we should use all our tokens before they run out. Why? Because everyone else is. We started measuring shovels instead of the hole. Someone’s needy little nerd booked their dentist, replied to their mum and launched a business whilst they were asleep. They’ve got an org chart. For nerds. With a Chief of Staff. You feel behind. Like way behind. So you grab a shovel and start digging. A little hole over there to triage your inbox, one here to draft your tweets, one to check on those. Then you spend your day checking the holes are being dug right. Before long, you’re surrounded by holes and a mountain of dirt you gotta do something with. Now as a man, holes are hardwired into my DNA. A few beers, a beach and a shovel, I’m digging a hole. I’d take pride in it. I’d make the best one, impressively round, deep enough to see sea water seep through the bottom. But I’d only dig one. There’s a whole beach but I chose this spot. Next time the needy little nerd pings you: do you really want another hole? Also, don’t dig big holes on the beach. They collapse. Nathan Lambert Nov 14, 2026 127 24 21 Share Article voiceover 0:00 -7:28 Audio playback is not supported on your browser. Please upgrade. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a major setback for the US development of an open model ecosystem. Nvidia still has the financial interests in supporting open models, which are to avoid concentration in power among a few customers who would develop their own chips and reduce Nvidia’s profits, but supporting the open ecosystem is a tricky puzzle more than an engineering problem to grind out a solution on. Nvidia’s business operations are famously extremely dependent on Jensen as an operator, so it is a consensus opinion that there are challenges ahead (or even more high-profile departures through chip-smuggling investigations or plain-old sharks circling more poachable talent). Nvidia’s number one goal is to stabilize the ship, deliver to customers in the next 24 months, and prevent implosion. Open models have been one of Jensen’s more ambitious, founder-style bets. He has been flooding the zone with funding in a way that will very likely dry up. Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Subscribe In this period, the open model economy is in its nascency. These are crucial years for establishing use-cases, revenue flow, and motives to continue training the next generation models. I discussed the sensitivity of these early years in my recent talk at Fireworks Forge ( slides , recording ). The core of the argument is one upside for open models, a reason to be optimistic, and one downside. The positive case is that the open model economy has correctly latched onto “ownership of intelligence” and enterprise post-training as a crucial lane. What is to be determined is exactly how big the downstream market is. The downside is that the true long-term benefit of open models, as truly commoditized intelligence, is very far from realization with compute in such short supply. In the near term, where inference startups are also struggling to get enough chips (because Anthropic and OpenAI are buying so much capacity), there’s little margin competition on open-weight models. If open-source models are also served at giant inference margins, as we learned with DeepSeek’s DeepInfer release, they’re far from a commodity. In this paradigm, the closed labs with better economies of scale and integration from model to datacenter and chips will win. I expanded on this challenge in my recent piece on the open model economy . Together, a lot still needs to go right for open models to be a meaningful economic engine.
